scope: Policy engine for Fortnite season, pass, entitlement-window and ranked lifecycle intelligence for France/Europe

principles.facts_vs_policy: The lifecycle ledger stores canonical observed facts. This engine defines derived state, actionability, projection, reminders and graph rules.
principles.independent_tracks: BR, OG, Festival, LEGO, passes, collaborations and Ranked run on independent clocks unless an official relation explicitly joins them.
principles.window_semantics: Purchase, progression, quests, reward claiming and ranked play are separate windows. Closing one window never closes the others by inference.
principles.grace_period_first_class: A pass may stop progression while reward claiming remains open. Represent this as CLAIM_ONLY instead of ENDED.
principles.no_boundary_inference: END_AT, SEASON_END_AT, NEXT_START_AT and RANK_RESET_AT never copy across tracks by adjacency or arithmetic.
principles.field_provenance: Every material time/window/relationship may carry its own source and evidence so one corrected field does not rewrite unrelated facts.
principles.stable_identity: track_id, milestone_id, window_id and calendar_uid remain stable across extensions, reschedules and official corrections.
principles.quiet_calendar: Persist more facts than are projected into Apple Calendar; projection is action-driven rather than data-driven.
principles.derived_rebuildable: next_action, closure_state, completeness, projection and indexes are derived and never override canonical evidence.

track_model_v2.track_version_rule: Increment only when a material canonical track fact changes. Derived-only recomputation does not increment track_version.
track_model_v2.aliases_rule: Marketing-name or localization changes become aliases/history unless Epic identifies a genuinely different product/season.

rules: A track may have zero or multiple windows; absence means UNKNOWN, not CLOSED.
PURCHASE close never proves PROGRESSION close.
PROGRESSION close never proves REWARD_CLAIM close.
QUEST_COMPLETION may close before, with or after general progression only when officially published.
BONUS_REWARD_CLAIM is distinct from base REWARD_CLAIM if Epic publishes a separate grace period.
OPEN/CLOSED states with no published clock may be stored without inventing opens_at/closes_at.
Extension keeps window_id and appends previous timing/history.

rules.FULLY_OPEN: At least one main progression/play window is OPEN and no material closure state dominates.
rules.PURCHASE_CLOSED_BUT_PLAYABLE: Purchase is CLOSED while progression/play remains OPEN.
rules.PROGRESSION_CLOSED: Progression/play is CLOSED and claim state is unknown or not independently open.
rules.CLAIM_ONLY: Progression/play is CLOSED but an official reward-claim window remains OPEN/future.
rules.FULLY_CLOSED: All officially known action windows are CLOSED and no successor transition action remains on this track.
rules.TRANSITIONING: Official downtime/successor handoff is currently active.
rules.no_unknown_collapse: UNKNOWN claim/purchase state cannot be converted to CLOSED just because progression ended.

next_action_engine.CLAIM_REWARDS: Official claim window is open/closing and progression is closed or claim deadline is the nearest material action.
next_action_engine.FINISH_QUESTS: Quest-completion deadline is the nearest active actionable window.
next_action_engine.EARN_PROGRESS: Progression window is active with an official future close or the track is explicitly active.
next_action_engine.BUY_OR_UPGRADE: Purchase/premium-upgrade window is actionable and user can still benefit before progression closes.
next_action_engine.PLAY_RANKED: Ranked play window is active with no more urgent reset action.
next_action_engine.PREPARE_FOR_RESET: Official reset is scheduled and future.
next_action_engine.WAIT_FOR_DOWNTIME: Official transition downtime is the next known action.
next_action_engine.START_NEXT_TRACK: Successor is officially scheduled/active and is the next action.
next_action_engine.no_user_entitlement_assumption: Do not infer whether the user owns a pass or has completed rewards unless a future explicit user-state layer provides that fact.

field_rules.pass_identity: Requires official pass/product/news naming; cosmetic bundles alone do not create pass tracks.
field_rules.start_at: Requires official date/time or explicitly usable availability window. Announcement publication time is not start time.
field_rules.end_at: Requires official end date/time. DATE_ONLY stays date-only.
field_rules.purchase_window: Only materialize when an official source explicitly distinguishes purchase/upgrade availability.
field_rules.progression_window: Only materialize earn/progression close when official wording establishes it; generic pass END_AT is not automatically progression close.
field_rules.quest_window: Quest deadline must be published for the quest/campaign scope; do not inherit from pass end by default.
field_rules.claim_window: Never infer claim cutoff from END_AT or progression cutoff.
field_rules.rank_reset_at: Requires explicit Ranked reset statement/date for the applicable scope.
field_rules.next_start_at: Requires direct official successor launch date/time; transition downtime may support but cannot replace content identity evidence.
field_rules.downtime_relation: Epic Status confirms service timing; lifecycle linkage needs explicit Epic/Fortnite relation.

time_semantics.exact: Store timezone-aware ISO-8601 and preserve source_timezone.
time_semantics.date_only: Represents a source calendar date, not 00:00 local time.
time_semantics.date_range: Represents an official bounded range without invented intra-day times.
time_semantics.window_only: A broad official window remains watch/ledger unless the window itself is useful for planning.
time_semantics.dst: Convert Europe/Paris using real timezone rules for the target date; never fixed UTC offsets.
time_semantics.source_date_guard: If a product page says a date in a source timezone but no hour, keep source_timezone-qualified DATE_ONLY.

rules: PASS_FOR_SEASON does not imply equal start/end times.
RANKED_FOR_SEASON does not imply reset at season boundary.
NEXT_TRACK/SUCCESSOR_OF may exist with unknown start time.
TRANSITION_DOWNTIME requires official service_event_id and lifecycle relation.
REPLACED_BY requires actual official replacement/activation, not announcement only.
SHARES_WINDOW_WITH can reduce duplicate reminders but never merges track identities.
SIGNAL_ONLY/UNKNOWN edges cannot create timestamps, calendar events or strong reminders.
A predecessor may end before, during or after successor availability; do not force contiguity.
GAP_UNKNOWN is valid and preferable to inventing a start time.
Downtime and content launch remain separate logical events even when linked.
HANDOFF_COMPLETE requires successor ACTIVE or explicit replacement evidence.
Separate scope tracks when Epic publishes different cycles or reset behavior.
A reset for one scope never propagates to another without explicit global wording.
NO_RESET requires explicit official evidence; absence of reset announcement remains UNKNOWN.
Ordinary Ranked Cups stay in the competitive ledger, not this lifecycle ledger.

anti_bazar: Do not create a VEVENT per reward page, teaser or cosmetic item.
If several officially distinct windows close at the same timestamp, prefer one logical VEVENT with X-FORTNITE-CLOSING-WINDOWS rather than duplicate cards.
If progression and claim close at different times, keep separate actionable milestones.
A successor launch already represented by a season event is not duplicated as a pass event unless timing/action materially differs.
calendar_projection_v2.grouping: Related pass end, downtime and successor launch may share calendar_group_id/RELATED-TO while remaining distinct UIDs.

reminder_policy_v2.semantic_coalescing: When multiple closure milestones share the exact same effective timestamp, coalesce reminders into one notice listing all closing windows unless one is materially more urgent.
reminder_policy_v2.extension: Keep IDs, increment canonical version, invalidate obsolete future notices and recalculate.
reminder_policy_v2.shortening: Replace future notices immediately and notify only when the earlier deadline is materially actionable.

deadline_bridge_v2.legacy: BATTLE_PASS_END_DATE remains accepted for the existing Runners event.
deadline_bridge_v2.calendar_deadline_sync: Matching lifecycle/calendar facts share track_id, window/milestone identity and source precision.

completeness_engine.rule: Completeness describes known lifecycle evidence, not product quality or user progress.
completeness_engine.no_false_complete: END_KNOWN does not become WINDOWS_COMPLETE when purchase/progression/claim semantics are unpublished.

index_contract.authority: Index is rebuildable and never overrides the ledger/engine.

correction_policy.material_correction: Preserve previous official value in history and increment relevant track/window/milestone version.
correction_policy.same_fact: Re-observing the same official value does not create history or a commit.
correction_policy.supersession: When Epic explicitly replaces one track/product with another, use REPLACED_BY/SUCCESSOR_OF and keep both identities.
correction_policy.cancellation: Cancelled milestones remain in history; projected VEVENT uses STATUS:CANCELLED rather than deletion.

notify: new exact/date-only actionable season or pass launch/end
silent: index rebuild with same logical content

history_policy_v2.anti_noise: checked_at/observed_at or derived-only state changes never append history by themselves.

rules: Keep all existing track_id, milestone_id and calendar_uid values.
Existing END_AT facts stay canonical and do not automatically generate windows.
Materialize windows/closure_state/next_action into the ledger only when a real business fact changes or a new official window is discovered.
Technical V2 metadata alone never increments ICS SEQUENCE.
